A.explanation: Length $L = RA/\rho$ gives about $1.20 \text{ m}$ when the correct circular area is used.

B.explanation: About $4$ times too large, obtained if diameter $0.280 \text{ mm}$ is used as radius when finding area.

hints: Notice you are given diameter $0.280 \text{ mm}$, so first find radius in metres before finding cross-sectional area $A = \pi r^2$.
Recall resistance is linked to geometry by $R = \rho L/A$, so rearranged length is $L = RA/\rho$.
Calculate $A$ in $\text{m}^2$ from $r = 0.140 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}$, then evaluate $L = 9.55A/(4.90 \times 10^{-7})$ and check the unit is $\text{m}$.
walkthrough: Identify the data: $R = 9.55 \ \Omega$, $\rho = 4.90 \times 10^{-7} \ \Omega \text{m}$, and diameter $d = 0.280 \text{ mm} = 0.280 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}$.
Find the radius $r = d/2 = 0.140 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m} = 1.40 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}$, then the area $A = \pi r^2 = \pi(1.40 \times 10^{-4})^2$.
Use $R = \rho L/A$ rearranged to $L = RA/\rho$ and substitute with units: $L = 9.55 \times 6.16 \times 10^{-8} / (4.90 \times 10^{-7})$.
Calculate $L \approx 5.88 \times 10^{-7} / 4.90 \times 10^{-7} \approx 1.20 \text{ m}$, which matches the value given. This is option A.
